synthesis: High-strip asymptotics and nonvanishing for the chi derivatives make it possible to divide the differentiated functional equation by chi^(m) and define J_m without introducing functional-equation-factor zeros. Zeros of J_m then encode reflected zeros of zeta^(m), so Littlewood's lemma converts their leftward displacement into a boundary integral while explicitly retaining a rightward zeta-zero displacement term. Fractional-moment control of successive logarithmic derivatives bounds that boundary integral, producing the comparison theorem; Selberg's estimate, functional-equation symmetry, and the cited signed total-displacement formula then respectively bound the left derivative-zero mass and isolate the right-side main term.
source_support: Unit u04 proves the fixed-strip chi^(m)/chi asymptotic and eventual nonvanishing and states the sublinear reciprocal-sum lemma. Unit u05 differentiates the functional equation, defines J_m, identifies its zeros with reflected derivative zeros, applies Littlewood, and bounds the resulting integral through local partial fractions, Lemma 3, and Holder telescoping. Unit u06 applies Selberg's zeta-zero displacement bound to Theorem 1 and combines Theorem 2 with the cited signed total derivative-zero displacement; unit u01 states the three resulting aggregate theorems and their interval scopes.
nonparaphrase_operation: Composes four source-specific changes of observable—chi normalization, reflection into auxiliary zeros, Littlewood conversion from zero geometry to boundary size, and decomposition of a signed total—to show how a zeta-zero estimate controls two directional derivative-zero masses.
limits: The conclusions concern weighted aggregate horizontal displacement, not individual zero locations. Theorem 1 allows every 0<U<=T, whereas the Selberg-based Theorems 2-3 require the stated long short intervals. The local partial-fraction and zero-count inputs, Selberg estimate, and total-displacement identity are cited inputs, and extraction-damaged fractions, signs, and secondary terms should not be reused without scan verification.
quality_reason: Accepted because distinct units jointly supply every link from gamma-factor control through reflected-zero comparison to the two unconditional displacement deductions; no single parent contains that complete mechanism, and the synthesis preserves the imported proof burdens and aggregate-only scope.

synthesis: Conrey's parameterized mollified mean square is a common variational interface, but two different auxiliary constructions determine what defect it measures. For derivative zeros, Littlewood and Jensen turn zeros of J_k on or left of the critical line into an L2 cost; integration by parts replaces J_k by V_k with Q_k(x)=(1-x)^k, and optimizing the mollifier makes the cost approach 2, yielding a right-side derivative-zero density approaching one as k grows. For distinct zeta zeros, the xi-plus-xi' auxiliary f deletes simple zeros and reduces each multiple-zero multiplicity by one; symmetry, Littlewood, and Jensen turn that excess multiplicity into the same kind of L2 cost, now with an admissible linear Q satisfying Q(0)=1, whose imported optimization gives kappa_d>0.70.
source_support: Unit u02 states Conrey's mean-square theorem for a Mobius-polynomial mollifier of length T^theta with theta<4/7 and a polynomial differential operator Q(-L^-1 d/ds), exposing the constant c(P,Q,R). Unit u07 derives the derivative-zero bound, proves the J_k-to-V_k mean-square replacement, chooses Q_k=(1-x)^k, and optimizes P. Unit u08 establishes the exact one-layer multiplicity behavior of f, relates its zeros to N(T)-N_d(T), rewrites f using a linear differential polynomial, records Q(0)=1, and invokes the optimized mean-square constant for the distinct-zero proportion.
nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies the auxiliary function and its differential polynomial as the semantic selector for a shared L2 instrument: one choice encodes derivative-zero side, while the other encodes excess multiplicity, so changing the operator changes the discrete zero statistic controlled by the same analytic theorem.
limits: Both conclusions are density bounds rather than pointwise location or simplicity results. The constants depend on the mollifier-length range, R, and restricted optimization family; the sinh profile in the derivative argument represents an infimum through polynomial approximation, while the distinct-zero argument requires Q(0)=1 and imports Conrey's numerical choice. Exact display-level normalizations and numerical parameters remain scan-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because the three units exhibit a concrete shared theorem-to-two-observables mechanism, with different auxiliary zero encoders and admissible operators producing genuinely different zero proportions; the relationship is unavailable from the imported mean-square theorem or either application alone.
